subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/timeouts from zephyr8b — mitigation & recovery plan
messages:
From: Liz Harper <liz.harper@brightpath.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: High 5xx and timeouts from zephyr8b since 08:45 PT

Hi team,

Since ~08:45 PT this morning our production traffic has seen a sharp increase in 5xx responses and request timeouts when routed to the zephyr8b model. It's not all requests but it affects roughly ~18% of calls and is causing downstream retries to pile up. Sample spans attached (error-snippet.txt).

Affected endpoints: POST /v1/generate (model=zephyr8b), streaming and non-streaming. We see both immediate 5xx and requests that hang ~10-20s then fail. Can you confirm if there was any change to model variants, kernel updates, or a routing policy change this morning?

This is impacting our customer-facing assistant on the main site — we may need to failover to a smaller model if this is going to persist. Please advise next steps and an ETA.

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Harper | Head of Product
BrightPath Labs

Subject: Re: High 5xx and timeouts from zephyr8b since 08:45 PT

Quick triage update (initial findings):
- Observed a correlated spike in kernel-level CPU stall and KV-cache cleanup loops across the zephyr8b serving clusters starting ~08:40 PT. Several workers reported transient out-of-memory indicators followed by 5xx gateway errors.
- We released a micro-optimizer for zephyr8b two nights ago that changes eviction heuristics for the KV cache; appears that under today's traffic pattern the heuristic caused aggressive cache churn and higher memory pressure.

Mitigation applied at 09:50 PT:
1) Rolled back the optimizer change on the zephyr8b image (reverted to image v2027-05-06).
2) Increased circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid premature trips while rollback completed.
3) Deployed short-term routing rule to redirect 30% of BrightPath traffic to zephyr8b-lite (lower memory footprint) and 10% to a pinned zephyr8b v2027-05-04 image as a safety net.

Impact so far: error rate for affected customer drops from ~18% to ~3% within the first 20 minutes of mitigation. We'll monitor for stability; if errors remain above 1% after one hour we'll widen the diversion.

Attaching interim RCA notes: rca-draft.md and our mitigation playbook (mitigation-playbook.pdf).

—Marissa

Date: 2027-05-09T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: zephyr8b elevated 5xx — recovery confirmed & next steps

Liz / BrightPath team — final update for today.

Summary of work completed:
- Root cause: a recently-deployed optimizer change to zephyr8b altered KV-cache eviction heuristics. Under BrightPath's request distribution pattern (long-tail prefixes + bursty batch calls) the change triggered elevated cache churn, higher memory pressure, and transient worker OOMs resulting in 5xx/timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation: rollback of optimizer change to image v2027-05-06, increased circuit breaker thresholds, and traffic diversion (30% to zephyr8b-lite, 10% to pinned older image).
- Recovery: as of 16:20 PT error rates have been within baseline (<0.5%) for 40 minutes across BrightPath's traffic. We have removed the temporary routing rules and are running a phased traffic ramp to pre-incident levels.

Next steps and deliverables:
- Full RCA document and timeline (Delivery ETA: 2027-05-11 17:00 PT) — will include regression test gaps and remediation actions for release governance.
- Credits: I've opened an SLA credits case for BP-8421 and looped Finance; procurement@brightpath.ai is on the thread. Expect initial credit proposal by 2027-05-12.
- Long-term fix: revise optimizer gating to include a traffic-shape regression test, add an automatic canary that runs a synthetic long-tail workload, and update our release checklist to require memory-pressure simulation for changes touching cache heuristics.
- Follow-up call: proposing 2027-05-12 10:00 PT to review RCA and credit proposal — please confirm availability.

We appreciate your patience and the sample request IDs which helped speed correlation. If anything reappears please message me directly and we’ll re-open incident response immediately.

Best,
Sean
